data.description:
## Symptom

An agent following AGENTS.md's orphan-prevention guidance **still leaked a process**: an orphaned
`zsh` reparented to PID 1, burning **87% CPU**, from a bounded contention run. It was caught only
because the agent independently ran `scripts/check_orphaned_load.py`; nothing in the prescribed
pattern reaped it.

This matters more than a single stray process. That AGENTS.md section exists specifically to prevent
a documented incident in which **38 processes orphaned to PID 1 and ran for four days** at ~1341%
combined CPU, pushing load average to 58 and silently poisoning every timing-sensitive measurement
taken in that window. Guidance that does not actually prevent the thing it was written for is worse
than none, because it produces confident compliance.

## Two independent gaps, both observed on 2026-09-04

**1. `timeout` does not exist on this macOS host.** AGENTS.md's primary bound is:

```sh
timeout 120 python -c 'while True: pass' &
```

There is no `timeout` and no `gtimeout` here (no coreutils). The command returns **127** and the
thing you meant to bound **never runs at all** — a silent no-op that looks like success. I hit this
myself: a command I believed was bounded simply did not execute, and I only noticed because its
output was missing. On a host where the primary bound is unavailable, every reader of that section
either fails silently or improvises.

A working substitute exists: `perl -e 'alarm N; exec @ARGV' <cmd>`.

**2. `trap 'kill 0' EXIT INT TERM` inside a subshell did not reap the wrapper.** AGENTS.md presents
the trap as the belt-and-braces sweep, saying it "signals the entire process group, so it reaps
helpers you forgot about". In the observed case the trap was inside a subshell and the surviving
process was the **wrapper**, outside the group the trap signalled. The claim is true only at the
right scope, and the document does not say what that scope is.

## Why this is worth fixing rather than absorbing

Every subagent brief in this repository repeats this guidance, so a gap here propagates to every
agent that spawns anything. Tonight it propagated to at least one, which then leaked exactly the
class of process the section exists to prevent — while believing it had complied.

Note also that `scripts/check_orphaned_load.py` **worked**, and is what caught it. The detector is
sound; the prevention advice is what failed.

## Acceptance criteria

Deterministic and verifiable in a single run — no "watch for orphans over N days".

1. AGENTS.md's orphan-prevention section gives a bound that **works on this repository's supported
   developer platforms**, macOS included. If `timeout` is retained as the primary example, the
   section must state that it is absent on macOS and give the working alternative alongside it — not
   in a footnote.
2. The `trap 'kill 0'` guidance states the **scope** it operates at and what it does not cover, or is
   replaced by a pattern that reaps a wrapper spawned from a subshell. Demonstrate with a real
   spawn/teardown that a wrapper does not survive.
3. **Defect-seeded:** run the documented pattern as written today on macOS and show the bound not
   taking effect (exit 127, command never runs); then show the corrected guidance bounding the same
   command. Both in one run.
4. Any check added is portable — no CI provider required — per the blocking `project.portability`
   criterion. `check_orphaned_load.py` is the model: read-only, on-demand, no CI dependency.

## Not in scope

Wiring an orphan check into `make lint`. `check_orphaned_load.py` is deliberately excluded because it
reports on **live host state**, not on the tree under review, and that reasoning is sound and
documented. This ticket is about the **prevention advice**, not the detector.

## File impact

`AGENTS.md` (the "Bound every background process you spawn" section).
data.title: AGENTS.md orphan-prevention guidance does not work on macOS: timeout is absent (exit 127, silent no-op) and trap 'kill 0' in a subshell left a wrapper at PPID 1
